name: 12 mm passive magnetic buzzer, PCB pins (Same Sky CEM-1203(42))
blurb: A small round buzzer with no built-in oscillator: it only sounds when it is fed a tone (a PWM square wave around 2 kHz), so it can play different pitches. It needs a transistor to drive it.

pins.note: The pin under the + mark on the case. Goes to the supply (3.3 V). Do NOT drive this buzzer straight from a microcontroller pin: the coil is 42 ohm and the datasheet gives 35 mA at 3.5 V with a 2048 Hz square wave, about 80 mA if the pin is left high, which is more than a GPIO pin gives. Use the datasheet circuit: an NPN transistor (base through about 180 ohm to 1 k from the PWM pin) switching the - pin to GND, and a diode across the buzzer.
The other pin, 6.5 mm from +. Goes to the collector of the driver transistor, not straight to GND and not to a GPIO pin.

verify: From the Same Sky drawing: 12.0 mm diameter, 8.5 mm high, two 0.6 mm pins 6.5 mm apart and 5.3 mm long, + marked on the case. This is NOT the 12 x 9.5 mm, 7.6 mm pitch outline of KiCad's Buzzer_12x9.5RM7.6: that pitch belongs to the common active (self-oscillating) 12 mm buzzers, while the externally driven Same Sky 12 mm parts (CEM-1203(42) and CEM-1206S) both have 6.5 mm pitch. Measure the pin spacing of the buzzer you have before making a board; the footprint named here is another maker's 12 mm, 6.5 mm pitch buzzer with the same pad positions. Unbranded passive buzzers are often 16 ohm and draw more: measure the coil with a multimeter. The body is a 1 mm placeholder plate; the real part is the cylinder. The sound hole diameter is not dimensioned on the drawing (3 mm assumed for the case opening). Peak current is calculated, 3.5 V across the minimum coil resistance of 36 ohm, for a drive pin stuck high; 35 mA is the datasheet maximum with a half-duty square wave. No bring-up pulse is set because the current is above what a pin may source.
sources: https://www.sameskydevices.com/product/resource/cem-1203-42-.pdf (Same Sky, formerly CUI Devices, CEM-1203(42) datasheet rev 1.05, opened and read: magnetic buzzer transducer, externally driven, rated 3.5 Vo-p, operating 3 to 5 Vo-p, max 35 mA at rated voltage 2048 Hz square wave half duty, coil 42 +-6 ohm, 85 dBA min at 10 cm; drawing: dia 12.0, height 8.5, pin pitch 6.5, pins 0.6 dia 5.3 long, + mark, sound hole in the centre of the top; application circuit with NPN transistor, 180 ohm base resistor and diode)
https://www.sameskydevices.com/product/resource/cem-1206s.pdf (Same Sky CEM-1206S datasheet, opened for comparison: 12.0 x 9.5 mm, also 6.5 mm pitch, 47 ohm, 45 mA at 5 Vo-p)
